name: Kanye West
hook: A Chicago producer whose sped-up soul samples made Jay-Z's 'The Blueprint', who then put Daft Punk and a drum machine at the centre of rap, and whose antisemitic statements from 2022 cost him most of his business partners.
blurb: Kanye West was born in Atlanta on 8 June 1977 and grew up in Chicago. He started as a producer for Roc-A-Fella. On Jay-Z's 'The Blueprint' (2001) he made beats by taking old soul records, speeding them up so the voices went high, and looping them, a style people called chipmunk soul, and he is credited with reviving Jay-Z's career with that album. In 2002 he was badly hurt in a car crash, and he rapped his first single, 'Through the Wire', with his jaw wired shut, over a sped-up Chaka Khan sample; it opened his own album 'The College Dropout' (2004). His 2007 song 'Stronger' is built on a sample of Daft Punk's 'Harder, Better, Faster, Stronger' and is credited with getting other rappers to use house and electronic music. On '808s & Heartbreak' (2008) he sang through Auto-Tune over Roland TR-808 drum machine sounds, and it had a big effect on hip-hop as many rappers copied it. He has named Stevie Wonder's 'Innervisions' and 'Songs in the Key of Life' as the albums he set out to compete with. From 2022 to 2025 he was widely condemned for antisemitic statements and for praising Nazism. Companies including Adidas, in October 2022, ended their deals with him over them. He changed his stage name to Ye.
